text:
Maya: quick thread — proposal for automatic model-variant switch when primary is saturated (capacity-based failover). want feedback on API, console UX, telemetry, and risks.

Jamie: Love this. Our customers keep asking for graceful degradation instead of 429s. key concerns: cache warming, correctness delta, and billing transparency.

Liu: Agree. Also need to think about per-tenant quotas + tiering. Higher-tier customers shouldn't be auto-swapped to lower-quality variants unless they opt in.

Ryan: Can we make it a policy attached to routes? like route.config.fallback = {mode: "auto", allowed_variants: ["quant-8bit","small-repl"], min_tier: "silver"} — then console can show which routes have it.

Anita: Console UX: expose a single checkbox "Enable auto capacity fallback" + a dropdown for fallback set. Add a tooltip: "Fallback will route traffic to compatible variants when primary is saturated; may affect quality." Add a per-route toggle for tenant opt-out.

Maya: +1 on per-route. My draft API snippet (very rough):

```
POST /v1/route_configs
{
  "route": "/generate",
  "primary_model": "redwood/longform-v2",
  "fallback_policy": {
    "type": "capacity",
    "threshold_pct": 92,
    "action": "failover",
    "allowed_variants": ["longform-v2-8bit","longform-v2-small"],
    "sticky_seconds": 30,
    "respect_tier": true
  }
}
```

Jamie: A few notes on that: threshold should be configurable by percentile (p95/p99) and by absolute queue depth. Also we need an explicit "cost_oversight" flag so finance teams know when we're routing to a cheaper variant.

Liu: Also add a "compatibility_hint" for variants that DO NOT share KV cache layout — so we can invalidate or warm caches differently. e.g., longform-v2-8bit might have a different cache format.

Ryan: Telemetry plan: emit events on every decision: fallback_decision {tenant_hash, route, from_variant, to_variant, reason_code: "capacity_p99", primary_latency_p50/95/99, time}. Aggregate metrics: fallback.count, fallback.rate_by_tenant_tier, fallback.latency_delta_ms, fallback.quality_regressions (tied to eval prompts).

Anita: UI telemetry: show a timeline on the route page with green ticks for normal, orange for fallbacks. Clicking a fallback event opens a pane with details + one-click rollback on the policy.

Maya: Security/compliance: ensure we tag fallback events with region and keep tenant identifiers hashed. For private deployments, default to "manual" fallback unless org admin enables.

devex-bot: NOTE: we should expose a test harness endpoint so customers can simulate saturating the primary and observe fallback behavior without real cost. e.g., /simulate_load?route=/generate&rps=xyz

Liu: Testing ideas: chaos load tests in staging + forced eviction tests on dedicated pools. Measure cache miss spike and quant-variant cold-latency.

Jamie: One tricky thing is KV cache compatibility. If fallback target can't use the same cached prefixes, we will see cold starts. We should add a "cache_compat" score on model metadata and use it in the decision.

Maya: Behavior options discussed:
- soft-evict: route a sampled % of traffic to fallback when near-threshold (gradual ramp)
- hard-swap: switch 100% when threshold crossed
- sticky: stick clients to chosen variant for N seconds to avoid thrash

Ryan: I propose defaults: soft-evict at p95>=90%, hard-swap at p99>=95%, sticky_seconds=20. Allow admins to change.

Anita: For billing transparency, add a usage label on traces and billing exports: fallback_variant=longform-v2-8bit. Also surface estimated cost delta in console.

Maya: Operational concerns: when fallback occurs frequently, route owner should get an alert: fallback.rate > X% over Y minutes. Add incident playbook: diag primary queue, check autoscaling, consider increasing reserved capacity for that tenant.

Jamie: API debate: should customers be able to opt-in per-tenant? we could allow route policies plus tenant_overrides, but that adds complexity. Maybe tier-based default: platinum -> off, gold -> soft-evict, silver/bronze -> auto.

Liu: Agree. Keep the first iteration simple: route-level policy + global tier defaults. We can add per-tenant overrides later.

Ryan: Implementation notes for runtime: decision path must be cheap. We'll add an in-memory token-bucket/queue-depth sampler per shard and evaluate policy without blocking the hot path. Decision result cached for sticky_seconds.

Maya: Edge-case: multi-request flows (chat with KV cache). If fallback breaks cache, we should prefer partial routing: keep short chats on primary, route long-running batch inference to fallback. Needs more thought.

Anita: UX for rollouts: let customers test on a % of traffic at the route level. Console toggle: "simulate fallback on X% of traffic" for 24h.

devex-bot: ACTIONS generated: create RFC doc, add telemetry event schema, wire up console toggles, runtime sampling hook, and a staging chaos test.

Maya: I'll draft RFC. Who wants to own telemetry schema?

Ryan: I'll take telemetry schema + runtime hook.

Liu: I'll take model metadata changes (cache_compat, quant_flag).

Anita: I'll mock console UX and rollout UI.

Jamie: I'll outline policy defaults and billing labels.

ops-bot: Reminder: on-call runbook update needed if fallback triggers frequent alerts.

Maya: Thanks all. Follow-ups: I'll post the RFC link here when ready. Short term: let's get basic API param and telemetry emitted in staging for a single internal route.

Ryan: thumbs up.

Anita: :raised_hands:

Jamie: lgtm

Maya: RFC: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/auto-fallback-1919909999 (draft)

devex-bot: Note: added roadmap ticket INF-3421 (simulate load harness)

Maya: closing thread — will ping when RFC is up for review.
